items.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: I took it and I did it for a couple of years... to be a part of that list... I hardly saved any money in those two years.

ctx.x: And you took an early detour from the studios to go with Woody Herman?

Yeah, that happened early on when I moved to Los Angeles, so I didn’t really — although I did do some studio work right away in L.A. I turned it down when they first called me. I’ll never forget it. It was in the evening and I had to play a gig. So during the gig I was saying I should take that Woody Herman thing. Not that I needed to move out of town but I think it’s a big deal because they called me to play first trumpet, lead trumpet, and the lineage of lead trumpet players that Woody’s had through the years…
Boy, when I was here, that kind of thing, the jazz guys, that was a goal. There wasn’t that many big bands left but boy we just, oh God, if we could go with Buddy Rich.
